page.title: Platforms to host virtual events: choose, budget, produce
page.description: Learn how to pick the right virtual event platform, match cost models, separate software from production, plan timelines, assign roles and connect follow‑up tools.
page.h1: What should you decide first about platforms to host virtual events?
page.definition: A virtual event platform is software that streams live sessions, manages registration, enables audience interaction such as chat and polls, and stores recordings for on‑demand access and analytics. It also integrates with marketing automation, CRM and reporting tools so that attendee data flows into nurture sequences and revenue attribution.
page.quick_answer: Pick a platform type that matches your format, then decide whether you need a per‑host licence, a monthly plan or an annual contract; West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: Which platform type matches my event format?

blocks.p: Choose a platform based on whether you need a simple webinar, a multi‑track conference, or a hybrid experience. The market splits into self‑serve streaming studios that you operate yourself, webinar licences tied to attendee capacity, and enterprise event suites that also handle registration, networking, analytics and on‑demand libraries.

ul: Webinar licence per host (e.g. Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams)
Enterprise event suite (e.g. ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast)
Hybrid‑ready platform with on‑site AV integration

sections.h2: What cost model fits my budget?

blocks.p: Platforms use three cost models: per‑host licences sized by attendee capacity, self‑serve monthly plans, and annual contracts quoted by sales. Matching the model to your expected volume and commitment level avoids surprise invoices and lets you forecast spend accurately.

sections.h2: How do I separate platform purchase from production?

blocks.p: The platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. Buying the software does not give you a live producer, a rehearsed show, or a safety net if the primary stream fails.

ul: Branded slide template and lower thirds

sections.h2: What timeline should I plan for a virtual summit?

blocks.p: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final. A webinar needs three to four weeks of preparation, including speaker briefs, rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before, and a technical check sixty minutes before go‑live.

ol: Speaker rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before
Technical check sixty minutes before go‑live
Replay delivery within twenty four to forty eight hours

sections.h2: Which roles and tools keep the show on track?

blocks.p: A summit needs six to eight weeks of management; a webinar three to four. Eight workstreams each have a single owner and a defined output, and they map to the seven stages from intake through reporting.

sections.h2: What integration and follow‑up tools should I connect?

blocks.p: Connect the event platform to your registration system, marketing automation, CRM and analytics so that attendee data flows into nurture sequences and revenue reporting without manual exports.

faq.q: Do I need a separate production team if I use a webinar licence?
faq.a: A webinar licence only provides the streaming engine; you still need a dedicated producer, a full speaker rehearsal, a redundant backup stream and professional post‑event editing to deliver a polished experience that reflects your brand. Without these elements the live session can suffer from technical glitches and low engagement.

faq.q: Can I run a hybrid event on a self‑serve platform?
faq.a: Self‑serve platforms handle the online stream but lack built‑in venue AV integration; you must coordinate on‑site cameras, encoders and a show caller yourself or hire a production crew. Without that coordination the hybrid experience can feel disjointed for remote attendees.

faq.q: What is the typical cost range for a moderated webinar?
faq.a: Moderated webinars generally cost two thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred per production, depending on crew size, rehearsal time and the need for a backup stream. Additional services such as custom graphics, multi‑camera switching and post‑event clipping raise the total.

faq.q: How quickly can I get the replay to attendees?
faq.a: Send the edited replay within twenty four to forty eight hours after the live session while the content is still fresh in attendees' minds. Prompt delivery also fuels follow‑up nurture sequences and improves conversion rates. A quick turnaround shows professionalism and keeps the conversation alive.

faq.q: Which integrations make post‑event follow‑up automatic?
faq.a: Integrate the event platform with your registration system, marketing automation, CRM and analytics so attendee data flows automatically into nurture sequences and revenue reporting. This eliminates manual exports, reduces errors and lets the sales team act on hot leads within hours.
